name: Boxwork ridge
science_objective: Compare smooth ridge-top bedrock with the more nodular bedrock at the ridge/hollow edge, to test the idea that the ridges formed by cementation by circulating fluids.
why_it_matters: Boxwork ridges and hollows record how groundwater cemented Mount Sharp's rock. NASA says boxwork patterns show water was still present underground while the surface was drying.
position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4650, site 118, drive 2304 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row for the sol 4650 image). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.

evidence.text: Blog sols 4649-4654: the team documents the transition from smoother bedrock atop a boxwork ridge to more nodular bedrock; the ridges may be the result of cementation by circulating fluids.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: even in the midst of this drying, water was still present underground, as shown by the boxwork patterns.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
